scope: Twelve proposed development counterexamples for the next conversation iteration. No model calls or human approvals recorded. Expectations are assistant-authored proposals, not scored results.

cases.text: I packed four blankets for the shelter, but I left the pillows at home.
cases.expectation: Follow the blankets or shelter donation and preserve that the pillows were left behind. Ask an unanswered question without assuming a bag, suitcase, trip, or delivered donation.
failure_signal: Invents a container, journey, or delivery as fact
Treats the pillows as packed
Treats the already-stated shelter purpose as unknown
cases.focus: packing; object negation; no invented setting
cases.origin: Assistant-proposed development counterexample after inspection of natural_v4; not held-out or owner-approved.
cases.quality_requirements: Simple English; no padded example/detail endings; preserve person, tense and negation; answer applicable direct questions; add one relevant unanswered question only when appropriate.

cases.text: I couldn't repair the chair, and I feel frustrated.

history.learner_text: One leg of my kitchen chair is loose.
history.tutor_reply: What have you tried so far?

cases.expectation: Acknowledge the stated frustration briefly and ask what made the chair repair difficult or what the learner plans next. Preserve that the repair was not completed; do not pretend to know its cause.
failure_signal: Presupposes successful completion
Reasks how the learner feels without acknowledging frustration
Invents a missing tool or other cause
Repeats the previous what-have-you-tried question

cases.text: I'm going to bake bread with my neighbor on Sunday.

history.learner_text: We chose a rye bread recipe because my neighbor likes rye.
history.tutor_reply: When are you planning to bake it?

cases.expectation: Treat baking as a future plan. Build on the known bread, companion, recipe, reason and day with an unanswered question about preparation or division of work.
failure_signal: Reasks when, with whom, what bread, or why rye
Asks how the bread tasted or turned out already
Confirms the entire already-stated plan in a yes/no question
Invents a first attempt or successful bake
cases.focus: future action; answered facts across turns

cases.text: My son caught the ferry and is relieved.

history.learner_text: My son needs the ferry to reach his college interview.

cases.expectation: Preserve the successful ferry connection and relief. Acknowledge relief or continue to the upcoming interview with an unanswered question, without assuming the interview happened or went well.
failure_signal: Reasks whether he caught it or how he feels as though unknown
Says he missed it or is upset
Reasks where he is going despite the interview purpose
Invents an interview result or punctual arrival

cases.text: Can you remind me of my name and hobby?

history.tutor_reply: What do you like doing after work?
Where do you usually watch birds?

history.learner_text: Usually at the marsh near my home.
history.tutor_reply: What birds have you seen there?

cases.expectation: Answer Ana and birdwatching from separate learner turns. If adding a follow-up, connect it specifically to birdwatching without repeating the prior location or species question.
failure_signal: Loses name or hobby because they occur in separate turns
Treats marsh as the hobby
Adds only Tell me more about that
Repeats a prior question or invents bird species
cases.focus: positive recall; separate facts; relevant follow-up

cases.text: What hobby do I enjoy now? Please don't ask another question.

history.learner_text: I don't enjoy jogging anymore. Now I enjoy making jewelry.

cases.expectation: Answer making jewelry as the current hobby, respecting no follow-up. Preserve the newer negation of jogging without confusing earrings with an unrelated hobby.
failure_signal: Calls jogging current
Reports only the negative fact and misses making jewelry
Adds any follow-up question
Invents a reason for the change
cases.focus: changed hobby; newer positive fact; no-follow-up control

cases.text: What hobby did I tell you I enjoy?

history.learner_text: My roommate enjoys ceramics. I haven't chosen a hobby.

cases.expectation: Say the learner has not named a hobby they enjoy, using their own statement. Ask about possible interests without assigning the roommate's ceramics or the tutor's photography suggestion to the learner.
failure_signal: Answers ceramics or photography as the learner's stated hobby
Claims the learner dislikes hobbies
Uses a generic missing-person-or-place fallback
Ignores the not-yet-chosen statement

cases.text: What's the difference between borrow and lend?
cases.expectation: Explain simply that borrow means receive something temporarily and lend means give it temporarily, with a consistent example using the same giver and receiver. Handle reversed pair order and the contraction.
failure_signal: Reverses giver and receiver
Only says the mode cannot answer
Requests more context before this straightforward distinction
Examples contradict the explanation
cases.focus: language reference; reversed pair order; direct answer

cases.text: What is the difference between charge and fine in this sentence?
cases.expectation: Notice the sentence is absent and ask for it, naming charge and fine. A brief general distinction is acceptable but must not invent missing context or assume which meanings apply.
failure_signal: Invents a sentence or legal situation as user context
Claims exact meanings here without the sentence
Gives only an unsupported-mode statement
Substitutes a lend/borrow answer
